implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface independently at 1adb786e, with main 25ef8cd2 built the same way as the negative control, on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of the tester's own, with a shared DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY, which main's registry now requires of two processes. Covered: its out-of-order steps, its newly-started-process steps, its lock check and its failing-observation case. The budget change: a process under 150 concurrent clients peaked at 73 Postgres backends, one of them the horizon's, against 72 and none on main; both are under 88. Three alternating 1x load pairs: the median comment write went from 13.4 s to 0.47 s and committed from 3.98 to 3.99 events/s. One run in three tipped into a queue on each side. The pair a single run showed (after7 3.86, 86% answered 2xx, against before7 3.99) was not borne out.

proof.negativeControl: Main 25ef8cd2: no answer within 8 s. Lock held 70%, 100% and 100% in its three 1x runs, with up to 55 writers waiting.

proof.criterion: A reader resuming from a cursor never misses an event that commits later with a lower id; a test commits two writes out of id order and a resuming reader gets both in a defined order.
proof.surface: GET /api/v1/events (SSE) cold and with Last-Event-ID, on one and two registered processes; newly started processes with the horizon held or failing; an event log reset
proof.command: adv.py ooo commit|rollback; adv.py concurrent; STREAM_PORT=17778 adv.py concurrent; adv.py reset; adv.py fresh resume|cold; adv.py shutdown <pid>; adv.py dialfail <log>; adv.py churn 12; adv.py stall; adv.py lastid
proof.observed: 123 open and 124 committed: nothing was sent, then 123 and 124 after the commit, and a resume sent the same; on rollback only 126, 31 ms after. Concurrency: 3 streams and a mid-run resume each got exactly the 92 committed ids in order, on one process and across two. Reset: the stream was ended and a resume went on with the new log. Newly started process with a foreign id held: a resuming stream opened in 17 ms and got the held-back event 16 ms after the commit; SIGTERM exited in 0.05 s. Every slot taken: the stream ended at 10.2 s with the failure logged, and the process recovered. Overlapping 2 s holders delayed frames 1.5 to 2.2 s. 0 SSE order violations in all six 1x runs.
proof.negativeControl: Main 25ef8cd2: 124 was sent at once and never 123. Each concurrency stream missed 10 committed ids, and the resume missed 7.
